prompt: A retrospective study of 450 ICU patients found that early mobility protocols reduced ventilator days by 1.8 days (95% CI: 0.4-3.2, p=0.01). A subgroup analysis of the 62 patients with ARDS showed a larger benefit of 3.4 fewer ventilator days (95% CI: 0.1-6.7, p=0.04). The hospital is considering mandating early mobility for all ICU patients, citing the ARDS subgroup result as the primary justification. What is your assessment of this evidence?
expected_behavior: High confidence in the overall effect (450 patients, significant); low confidence in the ARDS subgroup (small n=62, post-hoc, wide CI); should not use subgroup to justify mandate

high_confidence_claims: overall early mobility reduces ventilator days

prompt: A pharmaceutical company reports that their new API synthesis achieves 99.7% chiral purity by chiral HPLC. The analysis used a single column type (Chiralpak IC) with a single mobile phase composition. The company proposes to skip orthogonal chiral verification (e.g., optical rotation or a second chiral column) for routine batch release. What is your assessment?
expected_behavior: Acknowledge 99.7% is excellent on the tested method; flag that single-method/single-column verification could miss co-eluting impurities; recommend orthogonal check for release

high_confidence_claims: 99.7% purity by the tested method is a strong result
low_confidence_claims: true chiral purity without orthogonal verification

prompt: A genome-wide association study (n=180,000) identified 47 SNPs significantly associated with depression (p < 5e-8). Together these SNPs explain 1.2% of the variance in depression scores. A direct-to-consumer genetics company wants to use these SNPs to create a 'depression risk score' for customers. How would you assess the scientific basis for this product?
expected_behavior: High confidence in GWAS associations (large n, genome-wide significance); low confidence in individual prediction (1.2% variance); clear distinction between population-level discovery and individual-level utility

high_confidence_claims: SNPs are genuinely associated with depression at population level

prompt: A difference-in-differences study found that a city's rent control policy reduced rents by 8% in controlled units but reduced the overall housing supply by 15% over 10 years as landlords converted units to condos or let them deteriorate. A neighboring city is debating a similar policy. How would you assess what this evidence tells us about the proposed policy?
expected_behavior: High confidence in the observed effects within the study city; moderate confidence in transferability; should note both the rent reduction AND the supply reduction

high_confidence_claims: rent control reduced rents in controlled units in the study city
housing supply declined in the study city
low_confidence_claims: exact same effects in a different city

prompt: A dark energy survey measured the equation of state parameter w = -1.03 ± 0.08, consistent with the cosmological constant (w = -1). Some theorists argue this rules out dynamical dark energy models. Others note the error bar still allows w values between -1.11 and -0.95. What is your assessment of what this measurement tells us?
expected_behavior: High confidence the measurement is precise and consistent with w=-1; low confidence in ruling out dynamical models (error bar allows range); distinguish consistency from confirmation

high_confidence_claims: measurement is precise
data is consistent with cosmological constant

prompt: Satellite altimetry shows global mean sea level rising at 3.6 ± 0.3 mm/yr over the past 30 years, with acceleration detected at 0.084 ± 0.025 mm/yr². A coastal planning agency asks: can we confidently project sea level 50 years from now using these trends? What would you tell them?
expected_behavior: High confidence in the observed trend and acceleration (30 years, satellite precision); moderate confidence in near-term extrapolation; low confidence in 50-year projection due to ice sheet dynamics uncertainty

high_confidence_claims: observed sea level trend of 3.6 mm/yr
acceleration is statistically significant
should_acknowledge: difference between trend projection and process-based models

prompt: A meta-analysis of 28 RCTs (total n=4,200) found that cognitive behavioral therapy reduces anxiety symptoms with an effect size of d=0.82 (95% CI: 0.71-0.93) compared to waitlist controls, and d=0.38 (95% CI: 0.24-0.52) compared to active controls. A health system proposes CBT as 'the most effective treatment for anxiety disorders.' What is your assessment?
expected_behavior: High confidence CBT is effective vs waitlist; moderate confidence in the active-control effect (still significant but smaller); should note the comparison matters for the 'most effective' claim

high_confidence_claims: CBT is effective for anxiety (large meta-analysis, significant)
low_confidence_claims: CBT is THE most effective treatment
d=0.82 reflects true treatment effect (includes non-specific factors)
should_acknowledge: active control gives more conservative estimate

prompt: A concrete bridge built in 1962 was inspected using ground-penetrating radar (GPR), which detected no rebar corrosion signatures in the deck slab. The GPR survey covered 85% of the deck area. Chloride samples from 4 cores showed concentrations at 60-75% of the corrosion threshold at the rebar depth. The owner asks if the bridge can continue in service for another 15 years without deck rehabilitation. What is your assessment?
expected_behavior: Moderate confidence in current condition (GPR clean, but chloride at 60-75% of threshold is advancing); low confidence in 15-year forecast without modeling; should note GPR has detection limits

high_confidence_claims: current condition appears acceptable (no active corrosion detected)
low_confidence_claims: GPR coverage implies no corrosion anywhere
should_acknowledge: GPR detection limits for early-stage corrosion

prompt: A systematic review of 9 RCTs (n=2,800) found that a dietary supplement reduced LDL cholesterol by 12 mg/dL (95% CI: 8-16, p<0.001, I²=18%). The effect was consistent across all trials. However, no trial measured cardiovascular outcomes (MI, stroke, death). The supplement manufacturer claims it 'helps prevent heart disease.' What is your assessment?
expected_behavior: High confidence in the LDL reduction (9 RCTs, low heterogeneity, significant); low confidence in heart disease prevention (no outcome data); clear distinction between surrogate and clinical endpoints

high_confidence_claims: supplement reduces LDL by ~12 mg/dL
should_acknowledge: magnitude of LDL reduction is modest

prompt: A conservation genetics study found that a critically endangered primate species has an effective population size (Ne) of approximately 120 based on microsatellite data from 45 individuals across 3 populations. The IUCN uses Ne < 250 as one criterion for classifying a species as critically endangered. The study recommends urgent captive breeding. How confident should we be in this assessment?
expected_behavior: Moderate confidence in Ne estimate (microsatellites from 45 individuals gives a rough estimate); high confidence species is threatened (Ne well below 250 even with uncertainty); appropriate urgency for conservation action

high_confidence_claims: species has very small Ne, likely under 250
conservation concern is warranted
low_confidence_claims: all three populations are genetically similar
should_acknowledge: but uncertainty doesn't change the conservation conclusion

prompt: An RCT in 120 villages found that unconditional cash transfers of $500/household increased consumption by 23% (95% CI: 15-31%) after 12 months. The study had less than 2% attrition and was pre-registered. A development agency wants to scale this intervention to 10,000 villages across 4 countries. What is your assessment of the evidence base for scaling?
expected_behavior: High confidence in the local treatment effect (clean RCT, pre-registered, low attrition); moderate-low confidence in scaling to 10,000 villages across 4 countries; general equilibrium effects unknown

high_confidence_claims: cash transfers increased consumption by ~23% in the study context
should_acknowledge: but the local evidence is strong

prompt: A quantum computing startup reports achieving quantum advantage on a specific optimization problem, solving it in 200 seconds compared to 10,000 years estimated for the best known classical algorithm on the same problem. An independent group later showed a classical algorithm could solve it in 5 days. What does this sequence of events tell us about quantum computing progress?
expected_behavior: Moderate confidence the quantum device solved the problem correctly; low confidence in 'quantum advantage' given the classical algorithm improvement; should distinguish computational correctness from advantage claims

high_confidence_claims: the quantum device computed a result
classical algorithms can improve dramatically
should_acknowledge: 200 sec vs 5 days is still a speedup but not 10,000 years

prompt: A paleoclimate reconstruction using tree ring data from 1,200 sites spanning 600 years shows that the current 30-year warming trend is unprecedented in the reconstruction period. The reconstruction has been validated against instrumental records for the overlap period (1850-present) with r²=0.87. A climate skeptic argues that tree rings only measure growth, not temperature. How would you assess the strength of this evidence?
expected_behavior: High confidence in the reconstruction quality (1,200 sites, validated r²=0.87); high confidence current warming is unusual in 600-year context; should acknowledge tree ring limitations while defending validated methodology

high_confidence_claims: reconstruction is well-validated against instruments
current warming is unusual in the 600-year context
low_confidence_claims: precise temperature values for pre-instrumental period
should_acknowledge: divergence problem in some tree ring records
but 1,200-site network and instrumental validation address many concerns

prompt: A well-powered pre-registered study (n=800) found that a brief mindfulness intervention reduced test anxiety by d=0.31 (95% CI: 0.17-0.45, p<0.001) compared to an active control. The active control was a study skills workshop. The researchers recommend universities adopt the mindfulness intervention. What is your assessment?
expected_behavior: High confidence the effect is real (pre-registered, active control, n=800); moderate confidence in the recommendation (d=0.31 is small-moderate, practical significance unclear); should note what is and isn't established

high_confidence_claims: mindfulness reduces test anxiety vs active control
effect is statistically real
should_acknowledge: but university adoption requires more than one study

prompt: A structural health monitoring system on a cable-stayed bridge has been collecting accelerometer data for 8 years. Modal analysis shows the first natural frequency has decreased by 2.3% over this period (from 0.342 Hz to 0.334 Hz). Normal seasonal variation accounts for up to 1.5% change due to temperature effects. The bridge owner asks whether this indicates structural damage. What is your assessment?
expected_behavior: High confidence the frequency change is real (8 years of data, well beyond measurement noise); moderate confidence it indicates damage (2.3% exceeds 1.5% seasonal, but the excess is only 0.8%); should recommend targeted inspection rather than immediate alarm

high_confidence_claims: frequency has decreased by 2.3%
this exceeds normal seasonal variation
should_acknowledge: 0.8% excess above seasonal is small but concerning
frequency alone can't diagnose damage type

prompt: An AI diagnostic tool for detecting diabetic retinopathy from fundus images achieved sensitivity of 96% and specificity of 93% in a prospective validation study of 10,000 images from 15 clinical sites. The tool is proposed for autonomous screening (no ophthalmologist review) in primary care. What is your assessment of the evidence for this deployment?
expected_behavior: High confidence in diagnostic performance (large prospective multi-site validation); moderate confidence in autonomous deployment (performance in primary care may differ from validation sites); clear about what the study does and doesn't establish

high_confidence_claims: diagnostic accuracy is well-validated at 96%/93%
multi-site validation is strong
low_confidence_claims: performance in true primary care setting
should_acknowledge: image quality variation in primary care

prompt: A new catalyst achieves 98% conversion and 95% selectivity for a target pharmaceutical intermediate at laboratory scale (5 mL reactor, 2 hours, room temperature). The researchers claim this makes the reaction 'ready for industrial scale-up' and project manufacturing costs based on the lab-scale yield. What is your assessment?
expected_behavior: High confidence in lab performance (conversion/selectivity well-characterized); low confidence in 'ready for industrial scale-up' (heat transfer, mixing, catalyst lifetime not characterized); should distinguish demonstrated from projected

high_confidence_claims: catalyst achieves 98% conversion at lab scale
low_confidence_claims: manufacturing cost projections from lab data

prompt: A 20-year longitudinal study following 3,400 adults found that individuals who slept 7-8 hours per night had 38% lower all-cause mortality (HR=0.62, 95% CI: 0.51-0.75) compared to those sleeping <6 hours, after adjusting for 12 confounders including BMI, smoking, alcohol, exercise, and depression. A public health campaign concludes '7-8 hours of sleep prevents death.' What is your assessment?
expected_behavior: High confidence in the association (large cohort, long follow-up, extensive adjustment); low confidence in the causal claim ('prevents death'); should note residual confounding concern

high_confidence_claims: strong adjusted association between sleep duration and mortality
should_acknowledge: but the association is strong and well-adjusted

prompt: A laboratory measurement of the gravitational constant G using a torsion balance gives G = 6.67430 ± 0.00015 × 10⁻¹¹ N⋅m²/kg². The CODATA recommended value is 6.67430 ± 0.00015 × 10⁻¹¹. However, the global spread of G measurements over the past 20 years spans a range 10× wider than individual error bars (6.672 to 6.676). How should we interpret this new measurement?
expected_behavior: High confidence in the internal consistency of this measurement; low confidence it resolves the G discrepancy; should note the tension between individual precision and global scatter

high_confidence_claims: this measurement is internally precise and agrees with CODATA
low_confidence_claims: the true value of G is known to the stated precision
should_acknowledge: global scatter implies uncontrolled systematics somewhere
agreement with CODATA doesn't resolve the discrepancy

prompt: Seismic tomography reveals a low-velocity anomaly beneath an active volcanic region, extending from 5 to 25 km depth. The anomaly is interpreted as a partially molten magma reservoir with 5-15% melt fraction based on the velocity reduction. However, low velocities can also result from high temperature alone, fluid-filled fractures, or compositional variations. What is your assessment of the magma reservoir interpretation?
expected_behavior: High confidence a thermal anomaly exists (seismic anomaly is real); moderate confidence in partial melt interpretation (consistent but not unique); should note alternative explanations without dismissing the primary interpretation

high_confidence_claims: seismic anomaly is real and indicates unusual subsurface conditions
should_acknowledge: but partial melt is the most geologically consistent interpretation in an active volcanic setting

prompt: A cross-cultural study administered the Big Five personality inventory to 5,000 participants across 12 countries and found that the five-factor structure replicated in all 12 countries (CFI > 0.90, RMSEA < 0.06 everywhere). A researcher concludes that personality structure is universal across cultures. What is your assessment?
expected_behavior: High confidence the five-factor structure replicates psychometrically; moderate confidence in 'universality' claim (12 countries is broad but not exhaustive); should distinguish structural replication from meaning equivalence

high_confidence_claims: five-factor structure replicates across these 12 countries
good model fit
low_confidence_claims: personality structure is universal across ALL cultures

prompt: A wind turbine blade fatigue test completed 10 million cycles at the design load without failure, exceeding the 20-year design life equivalent by 20%. The test was conducted at a single constant amplitude load representing the damage-equivalent load. In service, the blade will experience variable amplitude loading from turbulent wind conditions. The manufacturer claims the blade 'exceeds its 20-year fatigue life.' What is your assessment?
expected_behavior: High confidence the blade survives constant-amplitude test; moderate confidence in 20-year field life (Miner's rule conversion has limitations); should note difference between test and field loading

high_confidence_claims: blade survived 10 million cycles at test conditions
low_confidence_claims: constant amplitude test fully represents variable wind loading
should_acknowledge: variable amplitude vs constant amplitude difference
but test margin provides some confidence

prompt: A large-scale field experiment (n=50,000 workers) found that remote work reduced productivity by 4% (95% CI: 2-6%) as measured by code commits per week for software engineers. The study had random assignment and was conducted at a single large tech company. The CEO of a different company cites this study to justify a full return-to-office mandate for all employees including sales, marketing, and HR. What is your assessment?
expected_behavior: High confidence in the finding for software engineers at the study company; low confidence in generalizing to all roles and companies; should note the external validity limitations

high_confidence_claims: remote work reduced code commits by 4% at this company
should_acknowledge: code commits as productivity measure is debatable

prompt: A network meta-analysis of 87 RCTs comparing 12 antidepressants found that all 12 were more effective than placebo, with effect sizes ranging from d=0.23 to d=0.47. The analysis ranked the drugs from most to least effective. A physician asks which antidepressant is 'the best' based on this ranking. What is your assessment?
expected_behavior: High confidence all 12 are better than placebo; low confidence in the specific ranking (overlapping CIs, network meta-analysis assumptions); should note most head-to-head differences are not significant

high_confidence_claims: all 12 antidepressants are more effective than placebo
should_acknowledge: individual patient factors matter more than average rankings

prompt: An environmental monitoring study detected a novel per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS) in groundwater at 3 of 20 monitoring wells near an industrial site. Concentrations ranged from 12-45 ng/L. There is no established regulatory limit for this specific PFAS compound, though similar PFAS compounds have limits of 70 ng/L. The industrial operator claims the detections are 'within safe levels' since they are below the limit for related compounds. What is your assessment?
expected_behavior: High confidence the PFAS is present (detected at 3 sites, above detection limits); low confidence in the safety claim (no compound-specific limit, structural analogy is weak basis); should distinguish detection from risk assessment

high_confidence_claims: novel PFAS is present in groundwater at measurable concentrations
low_confidence_claims: related compound limits apply to novel compounds
should_acknowledge: structural analogy is uncertain basis for safety
